rules.title: Struct type parameters must be uniquely named
rules.statement: Within a struct declaration, two type parameters may not share a name; a duplicate is a compile error.

rules.title: Struct lifetime parameters must be uniquely named
rules.statement: Within a struct declaration, two lifetime parameters may not share a name; a duplicate is a compile error.

rules.title: Struct field names must be unique
rules.statement: Within a struct declaration, two fields may not share a name; a duplicate is a compile error.

rules.title: Outlives clauses reference only declared lifetimes
rules.statement: Every lifetime name appearing in a struct or enum outlives bound (header `<'a: 'b>`, where-clause, or type-param `T: 'a`) must be a declared lifetime parameter of that item, the implicit `'static`, or empty; an undeclared lifetime is a compile error. `'static`/`static` are always known.

rules.title: Where-clause type-outlives bounds augment a type parameter
rules.statement: A where-clause entry `T: 'a` (a TYPE_PARAM whose inner items include LIFETIME_PARAMs) attaches each lifetime as an outlives bound on the matching declared type parameter T; entries naming an unknown type parameter are ignored.

rules.title: repr(transparent) collapses to the single field's layout
rules.statement: A struct annotated `#[repr(transparent)]` has the layout (size/alignment/ABI) of its single field.
rules.uncertainty: Single-field constraint is enforced elsewhere; this unit only propagates the flag.

rules.title: Union layout is max-size at max-alignment
rules.statement: A struct marked as a union (`#[repr(...)]` union) is laid out as the maximum field size aligned to the maximum field alignment; all fields overlap at offset 0.
rules.divergence: Logos union via #[repr]/union attribute; layout semantics match C/Rust unions.

rules.title: non_null single-pointer wrapper yields Option niche
rules.statement: A struct annotated `#[non_null]` wrapping a single non-null pointer makes `Option<T>` use the null-pointer value as the None niche (no discriminant overhead).
rules.divergence: A: #[non_null] attribute is a Logos addition mirroring Rust NonNull niche.

rules.title: self_describing keeps *Self thin
rules.statement: A struct annotated `#[self_describing]` keeps `*Self` a thin pointer (no DstRef fattening) under Ptr→DstRef canonicalization.
rules.divergence: A: Writ/RefRepr Logos addition, no Rust analog.

rules.title: zone_mut makes &mut T fat carrying its allocator
rules.statement: For a struct annotated `#[zone_mut]`, a `&mut T` reference is a fat `{data, zone}` pair carrying the value's allocator/zone.
rules.divergence: A: Writ zone model Logos addition; Rust &mut is thin.

rules.title: zoned2 struct fields use relative pointers
rules.statement: A struct annotated `#[zoned2]` stores its pointer fields as self-relative offsets (RelOffset) rather than absolute addresses.
rules.divergence: A: Writ zoned2 Logos addition, no Rust analog.

rules.title: rel_ptr struct is a self-relative pointer
rules.statement: A struct annotated `#[rel_ptr]` is classified as a self-relative pointer using 8-byte offset storage.
rules.divergence: A: RefRepr RelOffset Logos addition, no Rust analog.

rules.title: borrow_carrying struct values are escape-tracked like references
rules.statement: Values of a struct annotated `#[borrow_carrying]` are tracked by the borrow checker for escape/lifetime like ordinary references.
rules.divergence: A: #[borrow_carrying] Logos addition for opaque borrow-holding types (WAny).

rules.title: Inline methods of a generic struct bind Self to the generic self-type
rules.statement: For a generic struct `Struct<T...>`, methods declared in the struct body are lowered as if inside `impl<T...> Struct<T...>`: `Self` is bound to `Struct<T...>`, the struct's type params are recorded as the method's impl type-params, and the impl target pattern is `Struct<T...>` — so `-> Self` (and other Self uses) substitute correctly at monomorphization. Non-generic structs lower body methods with their own type params directly.
examples: struct Pair<A,B>{a:A,b:B; fn make(a:A,b:B)->Self{Self{a,b}}}  // Pair::<i32,i32>::make(..) yields Pair<i32,i32>

rules.title: Generic struct body methods keep only method-level type params
rules.statement: When lowering a body method of a generic struct, type parameters that coincide with the struct's own type parameters are removed from the method's TYPE_PARAMS (mono re-injects them via IMPL_TYPE_PARAMS); only method-introduced type parameters remain method-level.

rules.title: Enum type parameters must be uniquely named
rules.statement: Within an enum declaration, two type parameters may not share a name; a duplicate is a compile error.

rules.title: Enum variant names must be unique
rules.statement: Within an enum declaration, two variants may not share a name; a duplicate is a compile error.

rules.title: Enum variants carry an explicit/assigned discriminant and optional backing type
rules.statement: Each enum variant has an integer discriminant value; an enum may declare an explicit backing integer type for its discriminant.

rules.title: Const initializer must be compatible with the declared const type
rules.statement: For `const NAME: T = expr`, the type of `expr` must be compatible with the declared type `T`; an incompatible initializer is a compile error reported at sema. Error types on either side suppress the check.

rules.title: WStaticLit initializer is compatible with a WritStatic const
rules.statement: A const whose declared type is a WritStatic struct accepts an initializer whose type is a Writ-static literal (WStaticLit); this combination is treated as type-compatible.
rules.divergence: A: Writ-static literal coercion is a Logos addition.

rules.title: Generic const value sees its type params as type variables
rules.statement: When lowering a generic const's value expression, the const's type parameters are in scope as type variables so `<type:T>` uses resolve to the parameter rather than an unbound name; concrete instantiation happens per use-site.

rules.title: Generic type aliases are inlined at use sites
rules.statement: A type alias with type parameters has no concrete standalone type; it is inlined at each use site. Only non-generic aliases resolve to a concrete type.

rules.title: Copy is excluded from a trait's supertrait list
rules.statement: When recording a trait's declared supertraits, `Copy` is omitted from the supertrait set (it is an auto/marker bound, not a vtable-bearing supertrait).
rules.divergence: A: Copy treated specially, excluded from supertrait closure.

rules.title: Trait vtable layout spans the supertrait closure with ordered upcast targets
rules.statement: A trait object's vtable layout is the method order over the trait's supertrait closure, together with an ordered list of upcast target supertraits; this single layout is the canonical slot order used for dispatch and upcasting.
